pages.title: About
pages.content:
One room since 2011, seen by appointment.

One room since 2011

Nodo Clinic was founded in 2011 at 18 Veldstraat, 9000 Ghent, and it has never run as a walk-in surgery. Adults book, and one person has the room. A complaint of the ear, the nose, the throat or the balance is often slow to say out loud. A queue at the door would cut that short. Dr. Ines Vandermeer set the day up so that the person in the chair is the only name being seen.

The appointment line, +32 9 555 01 40, is open during opening hours, and you may also write to hello@nodoclinic.example. Children are not seen here. If you need a visit, you take a time, and the room is yours until that time is finished.

Why a first visit is 45 minutes

A first consultation is 45 minutes, in three parts of 15. The first part is for listening, before an instrument is picked up. The second is for looking at the complaint you actually came with. The third is for a plan you can say back in ordinary words. One patient stays in the room for the whole of that time.

The other lists are shorter because they are not a first meeting: a follow-up consultation is 20 minutes. The first visit is €95, the same figure as on the fees page. Length is not a promise about what the plan will contain. It is only the time in which the plan is made, at a pace you can follow.

Notes written by hand, at a desk by the window.

A morning huddle before the first patient.

Waiting, before the room is ready.

How the day runs

Rooms are set at 8:00. The first patient is at 8:30. Monday to Thursday the clinic is open until 17:30, and Friday until 14:00. The list is closed from 12:30 to 13:15. Weekends are closed. The appointment line is answered during those opening hours, and not outside them. Joris Claes, lead nurse, and Noor El Amrani, practice coordinator, keep the order of the book: linen laid out, names matched to the people who are due, and each person walked to the door when the visit ends.

Hearing tests and voice work sit inside the same hours, on the days those clinicians are in. Nothing is stacked over the midday close.

Adults only, by appointment. Mon to Thu 8:30 to 17:30, Fri 8:30 to 14:00.

Clinicians

First visit

pages.title: Complaints
pages.content:
Which complaints the room is set for.

Earache, wax, hearing and tinnitus

Two of the six rows on the home page belong to ears and hearing. Earache and earwax. An ear that hurts, or a blocked feeling that may be wax, is a reason to book a planned visit rather than to wait it out in a busy week. We look in the ear in the room, and wax can be removed in a separate 15-minute visit when that is the agreed step.

Hearing loss and tinnitus. When conversation takes more effort, or a sound stays after the room has gone quiet, the first work is to hear what the week has been like. A hearing test can then be booked as its own 40-minute visit. Dr. Ines Vandermeer holds this list on Monday, Tuesday and Thursday.

Ears and hearing

Nose, sinuses, smell and snoring

The next two rows belong to nose and sinuses. Blocked nose and sinus pressure. A nose that will not clear, and pressure across the cheeks or the forehead, are heard in one visit instead of being split into scraps. Bring the length of time it has been there, and whether both sides feel the same. Smell and snoring.

A change in smell, and snoring that worries you or the person beside you, sit on this same list. Dr. Samir Haddad is here on Monday, Wednesday and Friday. If a closer look is useful, a nasal endoscopy can be added to the visit. It is explained first. It is not sprung on you as a surprise extra.

Nose and sinuses

Headphones fitted in a sound booth, the door left open.

A head lamp is enough for much of an examination.

Voice, throat and swallowing

Hoarseness, swallowing and sore throat. A voice that frays, a throat that stays sore, and swallowing that has become difficult are one row, and so are people whose work depends on speaking. Say if you teach, sell, sing or talk for most of the day, because that changes what we book next. Dr. Lucia Ferreira sees this list on Tuesday and Thursday and looks with a small light while you are seated.

Helen Park, speech-language therapist, can see you for a voice assessment of 45 minutes from Tuesday to Thursday. The home page keeps the voice user inside this same row, so the complaint is not divided before anyone has listened.

Throat and voice

Dizziness and balance

Dizziness and balance. People rarely arrive with a textbook word. They say that they are spinning, that the room tilts, or that their feet no longer trust the floor. Those are the three plain descriptions we use, and a first visit is for sorting which one is yours. Dr. Tomasz Wrona sees this list on Wednesday and Friday.

When the conversation shows that a longer look is needed, a balance assessment is booked as its own 60-minute visit, not squeezed into the end of a consultation. Come by appointment, as an adult. The six rows above are the whole of what the rooms are set up to take.

Dizziness and balance

Adults only, by appointment. Mon to Thu 8:30 to 17:30, Fri 8:30 to 14:00.

First visit

pages.title: Ears and hearing
pages.content:
Ears and hearing, heard in full.

Earache, wax, hearing loss and tinnitus

The ears list is four complaints, kept together because they often arrive tangled. Earache may be the whole reason you call, or it may sit beside a blocked feeling you have been putting off. Wax is looked at in the room before anyone talks about a hearing test, so a removable blockage is not mistaken for a change in hearing.

Hearing loss, for us, means speech or everyday sound has become harder to follow than it used to be. Tinnitus means a sound that remains when the room is quiet. We do not rank these, and we do not tell you which one you ought to have minded first. A first consultation is 45 minutes: 15 to listen, 15 to look, 15 to plan.

What the room holds

The consulting room is set for one adult. An otoscope rests on a linen tray on the side table and is picked up only when the history has a shape. There is a pale sound booth with headphones for a hearing test, and the door can stay open while the headphones are fitted so the room is not a surprise. At a small table there is an unlabelled ear model, used when a sentence is clearer with something to point at.

Wax removal, when it is the plan, happens in this same room and takes 15 minutes. The instruments stay on the tray or in the hand where you can see them. You are walked to the door at the end of the visit.

An ear model on the table, shown before it is named.

Plain ear plugs in a small case.

When should I come?

Book when earache, wax, hearing loss or tinnitus is the thing you want time for. The clinic sees adults only, and only by appointment. Hours are Monday to Thursday, 8:30 to 17:30, and Friday, 8:30 to 14:00. The list pauses from 12:30 to 13:15, and the doors are shut at weekends. This is not a walk-in service and not an emergency department.

If you are acutely unwell, use the urgent care where you are, rather than waiting for the next open slot on this book. For a planned visit, call +32 9 555 01 40 during opening hours, or write to hello@nodoclinic.example, and say that the visit is for the ears.

The hearing test

A hearing test is 40 minutes and costs €70. It is not folded into the €95 first consultation. Amara Nwosu, the audiologist, is here Monday to Friday and fits the headphones herself. The test is offered when the consultation suggests it will add something, not as a hurdle you must clear before anyone will talk to you.

You sit in the booth, and the visit stays a conversation about the week you described: the meetings, the television, the voice you keep missing. We do not turn the result into a score you are meant to fear, and we do not promise a device or a recovery. A follow-up to talk it through is 20 minutes and €55.

Adults only, by appointment. Mon to Thu 8:30 to 17:30, Fri 8:30 to 14:00.

First visit

Fees

pages.title: Nose and sinuses
pages.content:
Nose and sinuses, looked at calmly.

Blocked nose, pressure, smell and snoring

Four complaints share this room. A blocked nose may have been there for years, long enough that you have stopped mentioning it. Sinus pressure may sit across the cheeks, between the eyes, or in the forehead, and it may not match the side that feels blocked. A change in smell is easy to skip in the story, so we ask about it on purpose.

Snoring belongs here too, when it has become a worry for you or for someone in the house. Dr. Samir Haddad sees this list on Monday, Wednesday and Friday. The first visit is still 45 minutes, one person in the room, with the same three parts: listen, look, and a plan you can repeat.

A flexible scope, coiled on linen until it is needed.

Waiting, before the room is ready.

What a nasal endoscopy is

A nasal endoscopy is a closer look at the nose, added to a visit. It takes 10 minutes and costs €60, on top of the consultation, and it is not sold as a first visit by itself. The instrument is a flexible scope. It waits coiled on a linen tray until it is needed, and there is no screen of writing for you to watch.

Before it is used, the clinician explains what it is for and why this visit needs it. A head lamp is enough for much of an ordinary examination. The scope is only added when that look is not enough. Nothing here promises that a blocked nose will clear, or that snoring will stop, because of those ten minutes.

When should I come?

Come when blockage, sinus pressure, a change in smell, or snoring is the reason you want a proper conversation. Adults only, by appointment. Say which of the four it is when you book, and mention if more than one is true. Noor El Amrani keeps the book and will offer a time on a day Dr. Haddad is in, unless you are already booked with another clinician for a different complaint.

The appointment line is +32 9 555 01 40 during opening hours. Email hello@nodoclinic.example works as well. Cancellation is free up to 24 hours before. The clinic is closed at weekends and from 12:30 to 13:15 on a working day.

Adults only, by appointment. Mon to Thu 8:30 to 17:30, Fri 8:30 to 14:00.

First visit

Fees

pages.title: Throat and voice
pages.content:
Throat and voice, listened to first.

Hoarseness, swallowing, sore throat and voice users

The throat list covers a voice that has become rough or thin, a sore throat that has outstayed a short illness, and swallowing that no longer feels straightforward. It also covers people who use their voice as the tool of the job: teaching, selling, singing, calling, reading aloud. Those are not separate clinics. Dr. Lucia Ferreira sees throat and voice on Tuesday and Thursday.

You sit, and she looks with a small light once the pattern of the week is clear. A teacher who fades every Thursday is a different story from a throat that has been sore without a pattern. Bring the pattern. A first consultation is 45 minutes and €95.

A hand on the ribs, to feel where the air goes.

Water and a blank notebook on the sill.

The voice assessment

A voice assessment is 45 minutes and costs €85. Helen Park, speech-language therapist, is here Tuesday to Thursday. It is its own visit. It often follows a consultation with Dr. Ferreira, rather than replacing it. You may be asked to do a simple breathing exercise, sometimes with a hand on the ribs so you can feel where the air goes.

A glass of water and a blank notebook are in the room if you want to mark what you notice. The point is to connect the voice to the day you actually work, not to put you through a performance. We do not promise that a tired voice will come back. We agree a plan you can try between visits.

When should I come?

Book when hoarseness, swallowing, a lingering sore throat, or a voice that your work depends on is what you want heard. If the voice is the heart of it, say so on the phone, and the coordinator can leave room for a voice assessment on a Tuesday, Wednesday or Thursday. Adults only. The line +32 9 555 01 40 is open Monday to Thursday 8:30 to 17:30 and Friday 8:30 to 14:00.

The clinic is not a same-morning walk-in, and it is closed at weekends. If you are struggling to swallow fluids or to breathe, do not wait on this book. Use urgent care. For everything else on this list, an appointment is the right door.

Adults only, by appointment. Mon to Thu 8:30 to 17:30, Fri 8:30 to 14:00.

First visit

Fees

pages.title: Dizziness and balance
pages.content:
Dizziness and balance, in plain words.

Three kinds of dizziness, in plain words

People use one word for feelings that are not the same, so the first part of the visit is translation. Spinning means you feel as if you yourself are turning. A tilt means the room seems to move, or to slope, while you feel still. Unsteadiness means the floor, or your feet, will not quite do what you expect, without a clear spin.

You do not have to choose the clever term. Dr. Tomasz Wrona sees dizziness and balance on Wednesday and Friday, and he will ask which of those three is closest, and when it shows up: on standing, on turning in bed, while walking, or in the middle of sitting still. A first consultation is 45 minutes.

Notes written by hand, at a desk by the window.

A clean otoscope, set on folded linen.

The balance assessment

A balance assessment is a separate visit of 60 minutes and costs €130. It is not packed into the end of a consultation. Part of the hour is talk. Part of it is a slow balance exercise on a mat, with the clinician close enough to steady you. Wear clothes you can move in. The assessment does not end by declaring that the feeling will leave, and it does not put a score on how brave you were.

It ends with a plan: what to watch, whether a 20-minute follow-up is useful, and what belongs with another of the clinic's lists, such as hearing, if the story points that way. One person is in the room. The door is walked to, every time.

What should I bring?

Bring a few lines, on paper if you like, about when the feeling starts and which of the three words fits. Bring the names of medicines you take. If you already have a letter about your ears or your balance, bring it only if you want it read. Wear shoes you can take off, and clothes that let you stand, turn and step slowly.

If you use a stick, or usually hold someone's arm outdoors, say so at the start of the visit. You do not have to arrive in sporting clothes. If the feeling makes travel difficult, book a time of day you can manage. Call +32 9 555 01 40, or email hello@nodoclinic.example, and ask for Dr. Wrona's list.

Adults only, by appointment. Mon to Thu 8:30 to 17:30, Fri 8:30 to 14:00.

First visit

Fees

pages.title: First visit
pages.content:
Forty-five minutes, in three parts of fifteen.

45minutes

15 to listen

15 to look

15 to plan

45 minutes, in three parts

A first visit is 45 minutes. The number is the whole method. Fifteen minutes are to listen. You describe the complaint, the week around it, and what you are hoping the visit will settle. The otoscope stays on the linen tray during this part. Fifteen minutes are to look. That may be the ear, the nose, the throat, or the first sorting of a balance complaint, depending on why you came.

Fifteen minutes are to plan. The plan is spoken in plain language, and you are asked to say it back so that nothing important is trapped in a phrase you would not use. One patient is in the room. The fee is €95.

What should I bring?

Bring the account you want to give, written down if you tend to lose the thread once you are in the chair. A few lines are enough: when it started, what makes it worse, and what you have already stopped doing because of it. Bring the names of medicines you take, and glasses or hearing aids if you use them.

If you have an older letter and you want it taken into account, bring that too. You do not need to prepare a medical history in anyone else's vocabulary. Come at the time in the book. Rooms are set from 8:00, and the first patient is seen at 8:30. The list is closed from 12:30 to 13:15.

The appointment line, answered at the desk.

A clean otoscope, set on folded linen.

An ear model on the table, shown before it is named.

How do I book?

Call +32 9 555 01 40 during opening hours, or email hello@nodoclinic.example. The line is open Monday to Thursday from 8:30 to 17:30, and Friday from 8:30 to 14:00. It is not open at weekends. Noor El Amrani, the practice coordinator, keeps the book. Say that you need a first visit, and say whether it is ears, nose and sinuses, throat and voice, or dizziness and balance, so the time offered falls on a day the right clinician is in.

The clinic sees adults only. There is no walk-in hour and no form to submit. A first consultation is the €95 visit of 45 minutes. Tests and assessments on the fees page are booked as their own lengths.

How do I cancel?

Cancellation is free up to 24 hours before the visit. Telephone the appointment line, or write to hello@nodoclinic.example, and the time will be taken off the book. If you need a different day, the coordinator will look again at the list you belong on. If you are inside 24 hours, still call, so the room is not left waiting.

The clinic does not publish a penalty charge, and this page will not invent one. What it does say is the part that is fixed: up to 24 hours before, cancelling is free. Hours stay Monday to Thursday 8:30 to 17:30, Friday 8:30 to 14:00, with the midday close from 12:30 to 13:15.

Adults only, by appointment. Mon to Thu 8:30 to 17:30, Fri 8:30 to 14:00.

Fees

pages.title: Clinicians
pages.content:
Eight people, keeping one list.

Who keeps the list

Eight people share one appointment book. Each is here on set days, and each list is kept to one person in the room.

Dr. Ines Vandermeer

Founder, ears and hearing · Mon, Tue, Thu

Dr. Ines Vandermeer is the founder, and she sees ears and hearing on Monday, Tuesday and Thursday. She opened Nodo Clinic in 2011 so that an adult could have one room for a full first visit of 45 minutes. Her list is earache, wax, hearing loss and tinnitus. She listens before the otoscope comes off the linen tray, and she uses an unlabelled ear model when a picture helps. Hearing tests themselves are Amara Nwosu's work, on a separate 40-minute booking. At the end of a consultation she walks the person to the door. New visits on her list are booked through the coordinator, on a day she is in.

Dr. Samir Haddad

Nose and sinuses · Mon, Wed, Fri

Dr. Samir Haddad sees nose and sinuses on Monday, Wednesday and Friday. Blocked nose, sinus pressure, a change in smell, and snoring are his list. A first visit with him is the same 45 minutes as everywhere else in the clinic: listen, look, plan, one person in the room. Examination is with a head lamp for as long as that is the right tool. When a closer look is needed, he adds a nasal endoscopy, 10 minutes and €60, with the flexible scope taken from a linen tray and explained before it is used. He does not keep a separate walk-in hour. Ask for his days when you call +32 9 555 01 40.

Dr. Lucia Ferreira

Throat and voice · Tue, Thu

Dr. Lucia Ferreira sees throat and voice on Tuesday and Thursday. People come with hoarseness, a sore throat that has stayed, trouble swallowing, or a voice their work depends on. She takes the pattern of the week first, then looks with a small light while you are seated. A first consultation is 45 minutes and €95. When the voice itself needs a longer, practical hour, she will say so, and Helen Park can see you for a voice assessment of 45 minutes. Dr. Ferreira does not promise that a voice will return to what it was. She agrees a plan you can describe to someone else after you leave.

Dr. Tomasz Wrona

Dizziness and balance · Wed, Fri

Dr. Tomasz Wrona sees dizziness and balance on Wednesday and Friday. He asks you to put the feeling into plain words: spinning, a room that tilts, or unsteadiness on your feet. A first consultation is 45 minutes and is only for that sorting and a first plan. The balance assessment, if it is needed, is another visit of 60 minutes at €130, with time for a slow exercise on a mat and someone close enough to steady you. He shares the building's rule of one patient in the room. Book his list by telephone or through hello@nodoclinic.example, and wear clothes you can move in if an assessment is the visit you were given.

Amara Nwosu

Audiologist · Mon to Fri

Amara Nwosu is the audiologist and is here Monday to Friday. She fits headphones and runs the hearing test, which is 40 minutes and €70. The booth is pale and quiet, and the door can stay open while the headphones go on, so you see the room before it is closed. She works with the ears list kept by Dr. Vandermeer, but the test is its own appointment, not a tail added to the €95 consultation. You do not have to arrive already knowing what you want from the test. Bring the situations that are going wrong: speech in company, the television, a sound that remains. She is not a reason to skip the listening part of a first visit.

Helen Park

Speech-language therapist · Tue to Thu

Helen Park is the speech-language therapist and is here Tuesday to Thursday. She leads the voice assessment, 45 minutes at €85, for people whose voice is hoarse, tiring, or essential to their work. A visit may include a breathing exercise, with a hand on the ribs so the movement is felt rather than only described. Water and a blank notebook are there if you want them. She often sees someone after Dr. Ferreira has already taken a history and looked at the throat. The assessment is practical and unhurried. It does not come with a promise that Thursday will sound like Monday. Booking is through the same appointment line as every other list.

Joris Claes

Lead nurse · Mon to Fri

Joris Claes is the lead nurse and is here Monday to Friday. He sets the rooms at 8:00, before the first patient at 8:30, and he keeps instruments on linen rather than in a scramble between names. Earwax removal, a 15-minute visit at €45, is nursing work inside that same calm. He walks people along the corridor and to the door when the consultation is over. He is not a separate medical list, and you do not need to ask for him by name to be looked after by him. If your visit includes wax, or you are unsure which clinician you are due to see, he and the coordinator between them will have the book straight.

Noor El Amrani

Practice coordinator · Mon to Fri

Noor El Amrani is the practice coordinator and is here Monday to Friday. She answers +32 9 555 01 40 during opening hours and reads hello@nodoclinic.example. A first visit, a follow-up, a hearing test, a nasal endoscopy added to a visit, a balance assessment, a voice assessment or earwax removal: she matches the request to the right length and the right day. Cancellation is free up to 24 hours before, and she is the person you tell. The midday close, 12:30 to 13:15, is kept empty on the book. Weekends are closed. She will ask whether you are an adult, because the clinic does not see children, and she will not offer a walk-in time.

Adults only, by appointment. Mon to Thu 8:30 to 17:30, Fri 8:30 to 14:00.

pages.title: Fees
pages.content:
What a visit costs, stated before you come.

Fees, in euro

€95a first consultation, 45 minutes

What is charged

Prices are in euro. They are not converted. The home page names only the first visit, and the full list is this one. Time is part of the price, because the book is built from these lengths and from one person in the room.

The endoscopy fee is added to a consultation. It is not a first visit on its own. Hearing, balance and voice assessments, and wax removal, are booked as the lengths above. A first consultation remains €95 even when the complaint is complicated.

Waiting, before the room is ready.

Will my insurer reimburse this?

Reimbursement depends on your insurer. Nodo Clinic states the fee before you come, and the figure you see here is the figure for that service. What you later receive back is a matter between you and your insurer. We do not publish a percentage, a tariff code, or a promise that any part of the fee will be returned. We also do not name insurers, and we will not guess your cover from a telephone description.

If you need a receipt in a particular form, ask Noor El Amrani when you book and she will tell you what the clinic can provide. Bring whatever papers your insurer has asked of you. The clinical visit itself does not change because of the paperwork.

How do I cancel without a charge?

Cancellation is free up to 24 hours before the appointment. Call +32 9 555 01 40 or email hello@nodoclinic.example and say which visit you are releasing. The coordinator will take it off the book. If you want another time, she will look at the days the right clinician works. Inside 24 hours, contact the clinic as well, so the room is not held for someone who cannot come.

This page does not add a late fee of its own. The only rule written down is the free cancellation up to 24 hours before. Opening hours remain Monday to Thursday 8:30 to 17:30 and Friday 8:30 to 14:00, with the list closed from 12:30 to 13:15, and closed all weekend.

Adults only, by appointment. Mon to Thu 8:30 to 17:30, Fri 8:30 to 14:00.

First visit

pages.title: Patient stories
pages.content:
Patient stories, composite accounts.

A teacher, 44

A teacher, 44, came because her voice gave out by Thursday. Monday still worked. By the last lesson on Thursday the voice was thin, and Fridays were spent rationing it. She told that shape first, before anyone looked. Dr. Lucia Ferreira listened, then used a small light with her seated. On a later day Helen Park did a voice assessment: 45 minutes, a breathing exercise, a hand on the ribs, a glass of water, a few lines in a blank notebook about which lessons cost the most. The plan was about how the teaching week was arranged. This account does not say that the Thursday voice recovered. It says she was heard at the pace of the problem she actually had.

Throat and voice

A cyclist, 58

A cyclist, 58, came because the room tilted. He was clear that he did not feel himself spinning. The room moved, mostly when he stood up from the floor at home, and he had started to dislike the moment after a long ride when he swung a leg down. Dr. Tomasz Wrona saw him on a Wednesday. They spent the first part of the visit on which of the plain words fitted. A balance assessment was booked for another day: 60 minutes, a slow exercise on a mat, the clinician steadying him, his ordinary cycling clothes left as they were. He went home with something to watch, and with no sentence promising that the tilt would stop. A follow-up, if he uses it, is 20 minutes.

Dizziness and balance

A couple, 71 and 73

A couple, 71 and 73, came about the television volume. They did not agree how loud it was, and each could quote an evening that proved their side. One of them had written examples on blank paper so the detail would survive the appointment. The first visit took 45 minutes and stayed with those evenings: which programme, which room, which of them was missing speech. A hearing test was a separate booking, 40 minutes with headphones in the booth, the door open while the set was fitted. This page does not report a winner, and it does not say the volume knob moved. Composite accounts stop before a result. What they were given was time, and a shared language for a disagreement that had become sharp.

Ears and hearing

A baker, 36

A baker, 36, had had a blocked nose for years. Early mornings and flour in the air were part of his account, but he had stopped telling people about the nose itself. Dr. Samir Haddad asked about smell and about snoring as well as about blockage, because those three share a list. He looked with a head lamp. A nasal endoscopy was added, 10 minutes, the flexible scope lifted from a linen tray after it had been explained. There was no screen of writing to stare at. The visit closed with a follow-up on the book, not with a claim that years of blockage would lift in a fortnight. He was walked to the door like everyone else.

Nose and sinuses

Are these outcomes?

Composite accounts. Results vary from person to person. Details here are drawn from more than one visit and then emptied of names. Ages and the shape of the complaint are kept because they are the point of the telling. Nothing on this page is an outcome we offer you or a typical result. The teacher was not promised her Thursday voice. The cyclist was not promised a level room. The couple were not promised agreement about the television. The baker was not promised a clear nose. Each story stops at the visit: a length of time, a person whose name is on the clinicians page, and a plan spoken in ordinary words. Your own visit stays yours.

Adults only, by appointment. Mon to Thu 8:30 to 17:30, Fri 8:30 to 14:00.

First visit

pages.title: Contact
pages.content:
Find the door, call the line.

Where and when

Nodo Clinic, 18 Veldstraat, 9000 Ghent, Belgium. The practice is fictional only in the sense that you are reading a theme demonstration. The facts we publish are the ones we keep: adults, by appointment, founded in 2011. Hours are Monday to Thursday 8:30 to 17:30, and Friday 8:30 to 14:00. Rooms are set at 8:00, the first patient is at 8:30, and the list is closed from 12:30 to 13:15.

Weekends are closed. The appointment line is open during opening hours and not otherwise. Come at the time written in the book. There is no waiting list you can join by standing at the door, and there is no weekend clinic hiding behind these hours.

Telephone and email

Appointment line: +32 9 555 01 40. Email: hello@nodoclinic.example. Noor El Amrani answers both, Monday to Friday, inside the hours above. Say whether you want a first consultation, a follow-up, a hearing test, a nasal endoscopy added to a visit, a balance assessment, a voice assessment, or earwax removal. Say which complaint, so the day matches the clinician.

Cancellation is free up to 24 hours before, by the same phone or the same email. There is no contact form on this page. If you write overnight or at the weekend, the message waits until the line is open again. We do not book children, and we do not offer a visit without a time.

The appointment line, answered at the desk.

Finding the door

The entrance is on Veldstraat: a pale brick front, white posts, a small tree, and a door without large lettering. Look for that quiet front rather than for a bright sign. Step inside at your appointment time and the coordinator will have your name. You will be taken through to one room, not to a row of chairs facing a counter of tickets.

When the visit is finished, someone walks you back to the door. If you are unsure you have the right front, call +32 9 555 01 40 while you are on the street during opening hours. We do not publish bus numbers, parking tariffs or walking minutes, because those change and they are not part of this practice's facts.

posts.title: Bring the shape of your week
posts.excerpt: The first fifteen minutes at Nodo Clinic are for the week around a complaint, before any instrument leaves the tray.
posts.content:
People often arrive with one word. Blocked. Dizzy. Hoarse. The word is accurate and still too small. A first visit at Nodo Clinic is 45 minutes, and the opening 15 of those minutes are for the week the word sits inside. The otoscope stays on its linen tray. Nobody is trying to win the visit by producing an instrument early.

The questions are ordinary. When did this start, if you can say. What changed in the day, rather than in the diagnosis you have been rehearsing. Which situations have started to go wrong. A hearing complaint may be the television, or it may be a meeting. A voice complaint may be the last lesson on a Thursday and nowhere else. A blocked nose may have lasted so long that you apologise for mentioning it. Those shapes matter more than a tidy label, and none of them needs specialist vocabulary.

On the ears list, wax, hearing loss and tinnitus are easy to tangle, including for the person who has them. Wax is looked at before anyone talks as if a hearing test were the only next step. The test exists: 40 minutes with Amara Nwosu, headphones in a pale booth, €70, booked on its own rather than clipped to the end of a consultation. It is useful when the history suggests it. It is not a toll you pay before anyone will listen. Tinnitus, if that is the word you use, is treated as a sound that remains when the room is quiet, and the visit asks what the quiet parts of your day are like. Earache is allowed to be the whole reason you came.

Nose and sinus complaints get the same unhurried start. Blockage, pressure, smell and snoring are four doors into one list, and Dr. Samir Haddad will ask about the ones you did not lead with. A nasal endoscopy is a 10-minute addition, €60, used when a head lamp is not enough. The flexible scope is coiled on a linen tray, it is explained before it is used, and there is no screen of writing for you to decode. Agreeing to it, or not yet agreeing, does not change the fact that the first part of the visit was for the story.

Throat and voice work follows the week just as closely. A sore throat that lingered, swallowing that has become awkward, and a voice that your job depends on are not three different buildings. Dr. Lucia Ferreira looks with a small light once the pattern is clear. If the voice needs a practical session of its own, Helen Park has 45 minutes for a voice assessment. You may breathe with a hand on your ribs, and there is water if you want it. The aim is a plan you can carry back into a real timetable. It is not a promise that a working voice will behave.

Dizziness needs translation before it needs a longer test. Spinning, a room that tilts, and unsteadiness on your feet are different feelings, and people often use one word for all three. Dr. Tomasz Wrona spends the opening minutes on which description fits, and on when it appears. A balance assessment, when it belongs, is 60 minutes on another day, with a slow exercise on a mat and someone there to steady you. Coming to the first visit already certain of the cause is unnecessary. Coming with two or three lines about the timing is enough.

Write those lines before you leave the house if you know you go blank in a chair. Bring the names of medicines, and glasses or hearing aids if you use them. Adults only, by appointment, at 18 Veldstraat in Ghent. The line is +32 9 555 01 40 during opening hours, Monday to Thursday 8:30 to 17:30 and Friday 8:30 to 14:00. A first consultation is €95. Cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before. You will be walked to the door when it is over. What happens after that varies from person to person, and this note is not a result you can claim.
